name: Palmoplantar keratoderma-XX sex reversal-predisposition to squamous cell carcinoma syndrome
aliases: Palmoplantar keratoderma with sex reversal and squamous cell carcinoma susceptibility

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse or focal palmoplantar keratoderma
46,XX karyotype with male phenotypic sex reversal
Increased susceptibility to squamous cell carcinoma, especially cutaneous
Family history consistent with X-linked or autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in the RSPO1 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of palmoplantar keratoderma, 46,XX sex reversal phenotype, and genetic confirmation of RSPO1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by genetic testing; early SCC surveillance recommended

pathognomonic.symptomName: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

laboratory: Karyotype analysis showing 46,XX with male phenotype
Elevated squamous cell carcinoma tumor markers in affected lesions
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI of gonads to assess dysgenesis or tumors
other: Histopathology of skin lesions showing hyperkeratosis and SCC features

distinguishingFeatures: No increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma
No predisposition to squamous cell carcinoma

redFlags: Early onset of squamous cell carcinoma in keratoderma lesions
Rapid progression or metastasis of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
references: OMIM Entry #618389 - Palmoplantar keratoderma-XX sex reversal-predisposition to squamous cell carcinoma syndrome
Smith FJ, et al. RSPO1 mutations cause palmoplantar keratoderma, sex reversal, and predisposition to squamous cell carcinoma. Am J Hum Genet. 2013.
